destination: Produce an implementation-ready specification for evolving the existing operator-driven shipment tracking bounded context into a multi-carrier, near-real-time tracking platform without breaking current order/shipment contracts or bypassing existing bounded-context boundaries.
out_of_scope: Choosing or integrating a real production courier account/credential in the discovery demo.
Production deployment or remote infrastructure mutation.
Replacing the entire order-placement saga or payment flow.
Implementing split-shipment fulfillment unless the decision map proves it is required by the destination.

fog.description: Carrier capabilities differ: some may push webhooks, some may require polling, and delivery guarantees are unknown.
The authoritative source of shipment state when operator state and carrier state disagree is not yet defined.
Duplicate, delayed, reordered and replayed carrier events may violate the current linear shipment transition model.
The meaning of near-real-time for operator/customer UX and the delivery mechanism to browsers are not yet fixed.
History/replay/backfill requirements and the shape of any tracking read model are unclear.
Authorization and data-isolation rules for exposing tracking beyond the current back-office API are unclear.
Migration from the current one-shipment-per-order, operator-advanced model to carrier-fed updates must preserve compatibility and rollback options.
Operational behavior during carrier outages, webhook loss, polling lag, poison events and replay storms is not yet defined.

decisions.name: Shipment truth and carrier boundary
decisions.question: What owns authoritative shipment tracking state, and what stable carrier abstraction lets webhook- and polling-based carriers coexist without leaking provider models into the shipment domain?

decisions.name: Carrier ingestion semantics
decisions.question: How should carrier updates enter the system across webhook and polling sources, including acknowledgement, retries, deduplication, idempotency and reconciliation after gaps?

decisions.name: Tracking state normalization and ordering
decisions.question: How should heterogeneous carrier statuses map into a canonical shipment timeline when updates are duplicated, delayed or arrive out of order, and which transitions remain valid?

decisions.name: Near-real-time UX contract
decisions.question: What freshness/SLO does near-real-time mean for operators and customers, and should browser delivery use polling, SSE or another mechanism given the existing Spring Boot/Angular architecture?

decisions.name: Timeline persistence and replay model
decisions.question: What durable model is needed for current state plus tracking history/replay/backfill, and can it fit the existing PostgreSQL persistence model without adding event sourcing unnecessarily?

decisions.name: Tracking access and privacy boundary
decisions.question: Who may read shipment tracking data, how does customer-facing access relate to existing operator roles, and what identifiers/data must never be exposed?

decisions.name: Carrier failure and recovery model
decisions.question: What operational recovery model handles carrier downtime, webhook loss, poll failures, poison payloads, replay storms and prolonged lag while keeping tracking convergent and observable?

decisions.name: Compatibility and migration path
decisions.question: How do we migrate from the current operator-driven one-shipment-per-order flow to carrier-fed tracking incrementally, preserving API/data compatibility and a safe rollback/forward-fix path?

decisions.name: Existing compatibility baseline
decisions.question: Which current shipment API, persistence, authorization, notification and frontend behaviors are already relied on by tests/contracts and therefore form the migration compatibility baseline?

ledger.statement: ADR 0035 models shipment tracking as operator-driven linear status advancement and explicitly has no real carrier webhook or polling integration.
The evolution must preserve current order/shipment API and persistence compatibility during incremental migration unless an explicit later decision supersedes that constraint.
Discovery and prototypes must not use production carrier credentials, deploy, push, merge, or mutate remote systems.
